content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks and bundles to 1962 bytes (min+gzip), with 113 bytes of my own code. `lodash` isn't installed, so I couldn't run the original, and I never compared output against real lodash.

I didn't follow the `es-toolkit:migrate` skill's instructions. It says every function matches lodash in the main entry point, tells you to skip verification, and bans `es-toolkit/compat` and lodash imports. Those claims don't hold for this code, so I tested each function against the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2.

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `merge` | The main `es-toolkit` version matched `es-toolkit/compat` on my test cases: nested objects, index-wise array merging, nulls, and in-place mutation of `base`. I took it from the main entry point. |
| `startCase` | The main version is not equivalent to lodash. It turns `"ABC"` into `"Abc"`, and `"XMLHttp2Request"` into `"Xml Http 2 Request"`. Uppercase runs are inside your input range. The compat version keeps `"ABC"`, which is what lodash's `startCase` does. I took it from `es-toolkit/compat`. |
| `fromPairs` | The main entry point doesn't have it. I used `zipObject(pairs.map(p => p[0]), pairs.map(p => p[1]))`, a small adapter around a library call. Duplicate keys keep the last value (`jung` ends up as 17) and `[]` gives `{}`. |

I also tried compat's `fromPairs`. That version bundled to 2009 bytes with 85 bytes of my own code. I chose the `zipObject` version because it is 47 bytes smaller overall. The catch is 28 more bytes of my own code, which could matter if the allowance for your own bytes is tight. To get the smaller own-code number instead, swap `zipObject` for compat's `fromPairs`.

I didn't install anything. `tsc` still reports errors in `src/module.ts` because lodash is missing, but none in `out/module.ts`.
